To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the variation of PRI in a field of view with the shadow fraction is affected (a) by canopy LUE and (b) by the diffuse sky radiation, and that the latter effect is of the same magnitude and shape as the former.
the effect of diffuse sky radiation on the relationship between PRI and the canopy shadow fraction is of similar magnitude and shape as the variation of the PRI with the canopy LUE.

the effect of diffuse sky radiation on the relationship between PRI and shadow fraction is of the same order as that of the photosynthetic down regulation, and therefore, it is not possible to remotely measure canopy photosynthetic down-regulation using PRI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of diffuse sky radiation on the relationship between canopy Photochemical Reflectance (PRI) and the fraction of shaded foliage.
the effect of blue light on the relationship between canopy shadow fraction and PRI.
the effects of the diffuse sky radiation on the PRI of a canopy, and how to separate the effects of photosynthetic light use efficiency from the effects of diffuse sky radiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
blue sky radiation causes a similar effect on PRI as LUE, which is difficult to separate.
the relationship between canopy shadow fraction and PRI is not suitable for estimating LUE.
the relationship of PRI with shadow fraction is not a reliable indicator for LUE, but it is a promising indicator of the photosynthetic down regulation of green leaves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PRI–shadow fraction relationship is a useful indicator for LUE, but it should be used in combination with other information, for instance, on the diffuse sky radiation, to be able to separate the effect of photosynthetic saturation from the effect of blue light scattering.
, in the case of diffuse sky conditions, the relationship between PRI and shadow fraction cannot be used to determine the photosynthetic saturation of a canopy.
the blue sky radiation effect on PRI is a potential source of error in the interpretation of remotely sensed PRI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of diffuse sky radiation must be taken into account in the remote sensing of canopy LUE.
the effect of the sky on PRI should be considered in studies using this parameter to estimate the LUE of vegetation canopies.
the effect of diffuse sky radiation on the PRI-shadow fraction relationship is large and cannot be ignored when interpreting PRI measurements in the field of a forest canopy.
